newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak says he refused to meet Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak says he refused to meet Netanyahu.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Saturday that he told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu the two leaders would not meet until Israel reaches a solution with the Palestinians on the West Bank town of Hebron.
Mubarak told a group of journalists and others that he informed Netanyahu of his position on October 4, just after the Middle East summit in Washington.
Mubarak had declined to go to the summit, on the grounds that it was clear that Netanyahu did not want to make progress.

Mubarak said that in a telephone conversation on October 4, Netanyahu briefed him on the Washington agreement to hold more meetings between the Israelis and the Palestinians on an Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.
The town, where 400 Jewish settlers live among 100,000 Palestinians, has become in Arab eyes a litmus test for the Israeli government's attitude towards Middle East peace.
Israel and the Palestinians agreed on arrangements for the town more than a year ago but Israel now wants to renegotiate the terms, arguing that the Israelis needs more security.
"Netanyahu said: 'You'll see within a week or 10 days, I'll solve something on Hebron'," Mubarak said.
"And I said: 'solve Hebron and I'll meet you. Short of that I won't be able to.' If he does a redeployment and adheres to the agreement, then he's welcome," he added.
"The situation is still complicated. There's no (Israeli) commitment to what was agreed," he said.
Mubarak's remarks were broadcast truncated on Egyptian state television and it was not fully clear if Mubarak's refusal to see Netanyahu still stood.
Mubarak will meet Israeli President Ezer Weizman on Monday.
